pass_a_gloss: For eye, he says, did not know, and ear did not hear, and upon heart of man it did not go up, what God prepared for those who love him. Then he shows what sort of affliction will be first against them. For through contempt, he says, of lips, and through another tongue. And such is the sense of the prophecy. In the Acts of the holy apostles it is written that: On the day of the Pentecost they were all together gathered at the same place, and behold there came from heaven a sound as of a violent wind being borne. Then it says: There appeared to them tongues being divided as of fire, and it sat upon each one of them, and they began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit was giving them to utter. For Christ had ordered them not to be separated from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, until they should be clothed with power from on high. Then having gone down they were speaking to those from Israel, and to all those from other countries, with the tongues given them by God, and those listening were astounded, and indeed were saying: Behold, are not all these speaking Jews? And how do we all hear, each in his own tongue, them speaking? And others said, it says, that they are filled with sweet wine, that is, they are drunk. This, I think, is the 'through contempt of lips, through another tongue'. For they were speaking in other tongues, the God who prevails in all things having foretold this too. For in other-tongued [men], he says, and in lips of others I will speak to this people, and not even so will they believe. But although it was needed to receive the sign for full assurance, having considered the foretelling made by God about this, this they did not do, but reproaching them with being drunk, they remained in disobedience. [Lemma, Isaiah 28:12:] Because they will speak to this people, saying to it: This is the rest for the one drinking, and this the crushing, and they did not wish to hear. God said somewhere, being vexed at the madnesses of the Jews: Behold I bring a famine upon the land, not a famine of bread, nor thirst of water, but a famine of hearing words of the Lord. And from east to west they will run about seeking the word of the Lord, they will not find. So a spiritual famine has been brought upon those from Israel, and since they did not receive through the faith the bread of life, the one come down from heaven and giving life to the world, for this reason indeed very fittingly they have come into want of the God-given food. For not on bread, it says, alone will man live, but on every word coming out through the mouth of God. And they acted outrageously toward the Saviour and Redeemer of all; but since he is good, although [Israel] having been impious not bearably, he was calling to change of mind [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: “For eye,” it says, “has not known, nor ear heard, nor has it entered into the heart of man, what God has prepared for those who love Him” (1 Corinthians 2:9). Then he shows what kind of affliction will come upon them first: “through contempt of lips,” he says, “and through another tongue” (Isaiah 28:11).

This is the meaning of the prophecy. In the Acts of the holy apostles it is written that “on the day of Pentecost they were all gathered together in one place, and behold, there came from heaven a sound as of a mighty wind rushing” (Acts 2:1-2). Then it says: “There appeared to them tongues dividing, as of fire, and it sat upon each one of them, and they began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance” (Acts 2:3-4).

For Christ had commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, until they should be clothed with power from on high (Acts 1:4; Luke 24:49). Then they went down and spoke to those of Israel, and to all who had come from other countries, in the tongues given them by God; “and those who heard were amazed, and indeed said: Look, are not all these who are speaking Jews? And how do we each hear them speaking in our own tongue? But others said,” it says, “They are full of new wine” (Acts 2:7-8, 13), that is, they are drunk.

This, I think, is the “through contempt of lips, through another tongue.” For they spoke in other tongues, and the God who can do all things had foretold this too: “In other tongues,” he says, “and with the lips of others I will speak to this people, and not even so will they believe” (1 Corinthians 14:21). They ought to have accepted the sign as full proof, bearing in mind the prediction God had made about it. This they did not do; instead they mocked the apostles as drunk and remained in disobedience.
“For they will speak to this people, saying to it: This is the rest for the one who drinks, and this is the ruin; and they would not hear” (Isaiah 28:12).

God once said, angered at the madness of the Jews: “Behold, I am bringing a famine upon the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the words of the Lord. And from the east to the west they will run about seeking the word of the Lord, and they will not find it” (Amos 8:11-12).

So a spiritual famine has been brought upon those of Israel. Since they did not receive through faith the bread of life that came down from heaven and gives life to the world (John 6:33), they have quite fittingly come to lack the food that God gives: “For man shall not live by bread alone,” it says, “but by every word that comes out of the mouth of God” (Matthew 4:4; Deuteronomy 8:3).
They behaved outrageously toward the Savior and Redeemer of all; yet because He is good, He called Israel to repentance, though it had been impious beyond bearing…

choices.why: Cyril reads the 'contempt of lips' as the mockery of the apostles at Pentecost.

choices.why: Acts 2:13; Cyril adds 'that is, they are drunk'.
The tongues were a sign that should have convinced them.
The famine of Amos 8:11 is of the word, not of bread.
